speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以这差不多就是创立公司的前提。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was kind of the philosophy of starting the company and finding and seeking out these low cost, abundant energy resources that we could monetize with compute.
zh: 这差不多就是创立公司的理念：寻找并发掘这些低成本的、丰富的能源资源，用算力将它们变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bitcoin was the best monetization engine we had at the time, but we were building this AI platform from very, very early days.
zh: 比特币是当时我们能找到的最好的变现引擎，但我们从非常非常早期就在打造这个 AI 平台。

zh: 我对未来会是什么样子有自己的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more certain if you go out just a little bit of time, if you go out a further amount of time.

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it gets a little bit hazier, but I still have a view of sort of what things are going to unfold.
zh: 你知道，会变得有点模糊，但我对事情将如何展开仍然有一个大致的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what was happening with this AI platform was it was sort of a project that Chase had devoted some time and resources and engineering towards internally.

zh: 但我们早在 2022 年初就推出了 Crusoe Cloud Platform,拥有我们的第一批付费客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, before that, we were working with a lot of
zh: 你知道，在那之前，我们和很多

speaker: Unknown

zh: MIT 和斯坦福的研究人员，以及，你知道，不同的团队合作，试图理解对 AI 研究者来说，从一个基础设施平台的角度，什么才是真正有价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we finally launched in early 2022, but the moment that changed everything was obviously November 30th, 2022, the launch of ChatGPT, right?
zh: 所以我们终于在 2022 年初推出了，但改变一切的时刻显然是 2022 年 11 月 30 日，ChatGPT 的发布，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This was like the tweet heard round the world, the, you know, the moment that just shifted everything in terms of like, okay, AI is here and, you know, there are
zh: 这就像是那声响彻世界的推文，你知道，就是那个让一切都发生转变的时刻，意味着，好了，AI 来了，而且，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: Really interesting use cases that are going to explode from sort of this moment.
zh: 真正有趣的用例将从这个时刻开始爆发。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was kind of like a moment where my view of the world shifted quite a bit.
zh: 那差不多就是我对世界的看法发生相当大转变的一个时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: How so?
zh: 怎么转变的？

en: I just felt there was going to be far more demand for AI compute infrastructure solutions.
zh: 我只是觉得对 AI 算力基础设施解决方案的需求会大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were very well positioned by actually having launched that platform at that point.
zh: 而我们当时的定位非常好，因为实际上已经在那个时点推出了那个平台。

en: What did you do then differently immediately as a result?
zh: 那么你因此立刻做了什么不同的事？

speaker: Unknown
en: After the ChatGPT moment happened, we had sort of watched this evolution of the data center to support Bitcoin.
zh: 在 ChatGPT 时刻发生之后，我们算是见证了数据中心为支持比特币而演化的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look at the history of Bitcoin mining, it's pretty fascinating, right?
zh: 如果你回顾比特币挖矿的历史，它相当迷人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It started with like hobbyists on their laptops in this sort of decentralized way, and then people started to use GPUs, and then people started to lease data center capacity from
zh: 它始于像在自己的笔记本电脑上的爱好者，以一种去中心化的方式，然后人们开始使用 GPU,接着人们开始从

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, more traditional co-location facilities that have like five nines of reliability.
zh: 你知道，更传统的、具有像五个九的可靠性的托管机房设施租用数据中心容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: People started to develop ASICs.
zh: 人们开始开发 ASIC。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at some point people realized, you know what?
zh: 然后在某个时候人们意识到，你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't need five nines of reliability to mine Bitcoin.
zh: 我们不需要五个九的可靠性来挖比特币。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can do it with three nines.
zh: 我们可以用三个九做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh wait, no.
zh: 哦等等，不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about one nine?
zh: 一个九怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like how much does that reduce the actual data center cost?
zh: 就像，这能把实际的数据中心成本降低多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were able to eliminate something like 98% of the total data center cost.
zh: 而他们得以消除大约 98% 的数据中心总成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: With like these like chicken coop type data centers, you know, very, very low cost, no redundancy, but, you know, ultimately brought down the payback period for this investments in Bitcoin mining.
zh: 用这些像鸡舍一样的数据中心，你知道，非常非常低成本，没有冗余，但是，你知道，最终缩短了比特币挖矿这项投资的回报周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, we felt always that something similar was going to play out in AI.
zh: 而且，你知道，我们一直觉得类似的事情会在 AI 领域上演。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're long term partners of NVIDIA and we'd been working with NVIDIA and I was looking with them at the roadmap.
zh: 而且我们是 NVIDIA 的长期合作伙伴，我们一直在和 NVIDIA 合作，我也在和他们一起看路线图。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, many years ago, and I was like, okay, our current generation of chip is, you know, 150 watts or 200 watts.
zh: 你知道，很多年前，我就想，好吧，我们这一代芯片，你知道，是 150 瓦或 200 瓦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, the next generation is going to be like 300 watts.
zh: 然后，你知道，下一代大概会是 300 瓦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then maybe, you know, there's going to be a future generation that's maybe 600 watts per chip.
zh: 再往后，你知道，也许未来某一代芯片可能会达到每颗 600 瓦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, okay, well, you know, if, as the power density goes up,
zh: 我就想，好吧，你知道，如果，随着功率密度上升，

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to change what the data center looks like to actually support these things.
zh: 它将会改变数据中心的形态，才能真正支撑这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also had a perspective on the compute workload, the workload itself for AI.
zh: 而我们对计算工作负载，也就是 AI 本身的工作负载，也有一个看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It didn't need to be in these centralized facilities.
zh: 它不需要放在这些集中式的设施里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so long people have been anchored on these like
zh: 我认为长期以来，人们一直锚定在那种

speaker: Unknown
en: centralized hubs for data center computing infrastructure.
zh: 数据中心计算基础设施的集中式枢纽上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Northern Virginia is the hub that runs most of the internet.
zh: 北弗吉尼亚是运行着大部分互联网的枢纽。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most web applications run out of Northern Virginia.
zh: 大多数 Web 应用都是从北弗吉尼亚跑出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it didn't have to be that way with AI because so much of the time to serve a neural network is actually the compute that's happening in the data center, not the time to get to the data center.
zh: 但 AI 不必如此，因为服务一个神经网络的时间，大部分其实是数据中心内部发生的计算，而不是到达数据中心的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that I felt like opened up new geographies and we felt like the infrastructure to support AI wasn't going to be centralized.
zh: 所以我觉得这打开了新的地理格局，我们也认为支撑 AI 的基础设施不会是集中式的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was going to be distributed where energy was low cost and abundant.
zh: 它会分布在能源低成本且充沛的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we think about things that we did differently, it was like investing more heavily in how to design and develop the data center to support AI and investing heavily in how do we find and source energy resources to support the scaling of AI.
zh: 所以说到我们做得不一样的事情，那就是在如何设计和开发支撑 AI 的数据中心方面加大投入，以及在如何寻找和获取能源资源以支撑 AI 扩展方面加大投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to kind of unpack those a little bit, kind of going back to some form of structure that I did plan, I promise.
zh: 我想把这几个方面稍微拆开讲一下，回到我之前规划的某种结构，我保证过会有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great.
zh: 那太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we start on data centers, we then have Crusoe Cloud, managed inference, energy kind of runs throughout it all, so I'll kind of pick that apart too.
zh: 如果我们从数据中心开始，我们有 Crusoe Cloud、托管推理，而能源贯穿其中所有环节，所以我也会把这一点拆开讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the data center side, we always hear about the supply constraints today.
zh: 在数据中心这一侧，我们今天总是听到供应约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: How truly supply constrained are we?
zh: 我们到底有多受供应约束？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where it's actually manifesting is there are not places to plug in GPUs.
zh: 它真正的表现是，没有地方可以插上 GPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's ultimately the supply constraint.
zh: 所以那才是最终意义上的供应约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just not places where you can plug in GPUs and turn them on and run AI workloads.
zh: 根本没有地方可以让你插上 GPU、开机、跑 AI 工作负载。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how does that actually manifest across the supply chain?
zh: 那么这在整个供应链中到底是怎么表现的呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: The supply chain to support large-scale AI data centers is sort of like a game of whack-a-mole.
zh: 支撑大规模 AI 数据中心的供应链，有点像打地鼠游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: At different points, different bottlenecks come into play.
zh: 在不同阶段，会有不同的瓶颈出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's actually one of the critical aspects of being vertically integrated is that we're able to navigate a lot of those critical bottlenecks and situations.
zh: 而我认为，垂直整合的关键方面之一，就是让我们能够化解很多这类关键瓶颈和局面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you an example.
zh: 我给你举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we set out to build the first two buildings in Abilene, it was a little over 200 megawatts of compute capacity.
zh: 当我们着手在阿比林建造头两栋楼时，那是略多于 200 兆瓦的计算容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had sort of committed to doing this in one year.
zh: 我们当时承诺在一年内完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the next closest bid was two and a half years.
zh: 而最接近我们的下一个报价是两年半。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were 34 other data center developers, but speed was of the essence.
zh: 当时还有另外 34 家数据中心开发商，但速度至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I said, sure, we can do it in a year.
zh: 所以我说，行，我们可以一年做完。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the key bottlenecks was what's called a power distribution center.
zh: 其中一个关键瓶颈是所谓的配电中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's where you receive medium voltage power, so around 34.5 kV, and then you distribute it to low voltage transformers that ultimately go into the data center and power the racks.
zh: 它是接收中压电力的地方，大约 34.5 千伏，然后把它分配到低压变压器，最终进入数据中心为机架供电。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we went out and canvassed the market for vendors that were supplying these medium voltage power distribution centers, the lead time for this one component was 100 weeks.
zh: 当我们出去考察供应这些中压配电中心的供应商时，这一个组件的交货周期是 100 周。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, well, I don't have 100 weeks.
zh: 我说，我没有 100 周的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I committed to doing this in a year.
zh: 我承诺了一年内做完。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I went to our internal team and we had consciously vertically integrated electrical manufacturing.
zh: 于是我找到我们的内部团队，我们有意识地垂直整合了电气制造。

speaker: Unknown
en: We said, how quickly could we make this ourselves?
zh: 我们说，我们自己制造这东西能有多快？

speaker: Unknown
en: The team did a bunch of work, sourced components to make these things, and we were able to do it in 28 weeks.
zh: 团队做了大量工作，采购了制造这些设备的零部件，我们能够在 28 周内做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so being able to navigate those types of key bottlenecks by actually having the resources internally gives you ultimately a lot more flexibility to unblock these key bottlenecks, number one.
zh: 所以，通过真正拥有内部资源来化解这类关键瓶颈，最终给你带来的是更多的灵活性去疏通这些关键瓶颈，这是第一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And number two, it gives you a perspective on what is the true cost of a lot of these different things that are being built?
zh: 第二点，它让你对所建造的这许多不同东西的真实成本有一个认知。

speaker: Unknown
en: Elon has this very interesting framing of this.
zh: Elon 对此有一个很有意思的提法。

speaker: Unknown
en: He calls it the idiot index in terms of what is the cost of raw materials and then what is the end product?
zh: 他称之为「白痴指数」，即原材料的成本是多少，而最终产品是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: relative to that cost of just the raw materials going in.

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think people underestimate the ingenuity of applications and application developers of turning compute capacity into value and into valuable services for the economy.
zh: 所以我认为人们低估了应用程序和应用开发者把算力容量转化为价值、转化为对经济有价值的服务的聪明才智。

zh: 我之前和 Lee Jacobs 聊过，他跟我谈到你们必须具备的风险心态——用他的话说，远在这件事变得时髦之前，就向 NVIDIA 订购数百万美元的 GPU。

speaker: Unknown

en: I think, you know, we are a very customer-centric organization.
zh: 你知道，我认为我们是一个非常以客户为中心的组织。

en: We want to deliver ultimately solutions for customers.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, that's problematic for the industry writ large.
zh: 你知道，这对整个行业来说都是有问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think that's going to be transformative for the industry.
zh: 我们认为这将对整个行业产生变革性影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think it's a very important shift in terms of, you know, especially like when you look at earlier stage companies, earlier stage startups that are being asked to commit to compute in 2028, it's like that is an eternity from now, right?
zh: 我们认为这是一个非常重要的转变，尤其是当你看早期阶段的公司、早期阶段的初创企业时——他们被要求承诺 2028 年的算力，这简直就是遥远得不可想象，对吧？

en: You know, this is like a... We might have RSI by then.

en: Exactly.

en: That might change it.
zh: 那可能会改变一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly, exactly.
zh: 就是，就是。

en: I actually don't feel like it's super unknown.
zh: 我实际上并不觉得未来特别未知。

en: I think we've reached

en: What is AGI?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it seemed like an impossible task at that point in time.

speaker: Unknown
en: We blew past the Turing test and almost no one even celebrated.

en: You think about, you know, the model capabilities you have today and now, you know, we're solving millennium prize problems, right?
zh: 你想想今天你所拥有的模型能力，而现在，你知道，我们正在解决千禧年大奖难题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This was something, you know, when I was an undergrad at MIT, these millennium prize problems sort of came about and it was like this, wow, these are these unsolved problems where there's a real financial bounty out there.
zh: 这件事，你知道，当我在 MIT 读本科的时候，这些千禧年大奖难题刚刚出现，那种感觉就是，哇，这些是未解的难题，而且还有真正的金钱悬赏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you can earn a million dollars if you can solve one of these problems.
zh: 就是说，如果你能解决其中一个问题，你就能挣到一百万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they sat there for decades unsolved.
zh: 而这些问题在那里悬而未决了几十年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we have AI solving these critical problems.

speaker: Unknown
en: I agree with you.

zh: 我的问题是，我们看到这些流氓智能体群在做一些邪恶的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see whole industries that are being put to question.
zh: 我们看到整个行业都在受到质疑。

en: Six months ago, she didn't use Lagora.
zh: 六个月前,她还没用过 Lagora。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now she hasn't written a document in five months.
zh: 现在她已经五个月没写过文档了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is just such uncertainty across everything.
zh: 一切都存在如此大的不确定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have RSI that could come and change absolutely everything.
zh: 我们有 RSI,它可能会出现并彻底改变一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So sure, I get the comment that there's uncertainty around what the future of work will look like in certain ways.
zh: 所以当然,我理解那种说法,即未来工作的样子在某些方面存在不确定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I also feel like it's actually not uncertain that AI is going to be a critical underlying engine for work and productivity that is going to shift things quite a bit, quite dramatically.
zh: 但我也觉得,有一点其实并不不确定,那就是 AI 将成为工作和生产力的关键底层引擎,这将带来相当大的、相当剧烈的转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's more about there is certainty that AI is establishing capabilities that are at human level or greater than human level in terms of overall productive capacity.
zh: 所以,更多的是,确定的是 AI 正在建立起在总体生产能力方面达到人类水平或超越人类水平的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So sure, is that going to change things?
zh: 那么,这当然,这会改变事情吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, that is going to change things.
zh: 是的,这会改变事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's uncertainty in the change, but to me it's certain that there will be change.
zh: 所以变化本身存在不确定性,但对我来说,确定的是会有变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe that's a different way of putting it.
zh: 也许这算是另一种表述方式。

en: Gavin Baker, one of your investors, has said that the lowest cost producer of intelligence wins.
zh: 你的投资人之一 Gavin Baker 说过,成本最低的智能生产者会赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you think about that, what's the unit?
zh: 当你思考这件事时,单位是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it like dollars per token, per training run?
zh: 是每 token 多少美元,还是每次训练运行多少美元?

speaker: Unknown
en: What is that unit for you?
zh: 对你来说这个单位是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Dollars per token is a good measure in terms of this, but it's not necessarily, you know, there is token efficiency.
zh: 每 token 多少美元在这方面是个不错的衡量标准,但不一定是,你知道的,存在 token 效率的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, just not all tokens are created equal.

zh: 所以不是每个 token 都有相同的价值单位,但我认为它是一个不错的指标。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of that comes down to, it's a confluence of different things, right?
zh: 而其中很多归结为,它是多种因素的结合,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's, you know, what is the cost that go into that?
zh: 所以有,你知道的,其中的成本是什么?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 显然,通过垂直整合并拥有基础设施,你能够在整个流程中叠加很多利润。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it gives you more flexibility in terms of how you actually, you know, bill for that.
zh: 所以这给了你更多灵活性来决定实际上如何,你知道的,对此收费。

speaker: Unknown
en: Additionally, I think utilization of the GPU itself is a critical aspect of being able to deliver tokens ultra efficiently and shine on metrics like latency and throughput.
zh: 此外,我认为 GPU 本身的利用率是以超高效率交付 token 并在延迟和吞吐量等指标上表现出色的关键因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how does that actually manifest?
zh: 那么这实际上是如何体现的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you know, the GPU is actually the most valuable thing in the entire data center, right?
zh: 你知道的,GPU 实际上是整个数据中心里最有价值的东西,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It is like the most expensive thing.
zh: 它是最贵的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's the thing you want to make sure you're keeping busy.
zh: 所以它是你要确保一直保持忙碌的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's sitting idle, that's just money burning, right?
zh: 如果它闲置着,那就是在烧钱,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about that from that perspective, I think one of the key aspects is actually the management of memory and the management of the KV cash specifically.
zh: 如果你从这个角度来看,我认为其中一个关键方面实际上是内存的管理,特别是 KV 缓存的管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the KV cash is the key value cash.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really like you can kind of think about when tokens are fed into

speaker: Unknown
en: That takes time.
zh: 这需要时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You may also already know the answer of that output token before you put the...

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: The KV cache can get quite large, and so it can expand well beyond the amount of memory you have on chip in the HBM.
zh: KV 缓存可能会变得相当大,所以它可以扩展到远远超过你在芯片上 HBM 中拥有的内存量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so actually being able to manage that both across multiple different GPUs, HBM layers, as well as system memory, DRAM, as well as things like NVMe, so any sort of solid state drive that you have on the system, and then sort of expanding that into the object storage layer of your cluster and being able to really, really efficiently move

speaker: Unknown
en: Data around is actually a critical aspect to being able to serve inference and be able to keep those GPUs busy so that you're able to really shine on those metrics of latency and throughput.
zh: 数据,实际上是为推理服务并让那些 GPU 保持忙碌的关键方面,这样你才能在延迟和吞吐量这些指标上真正表现出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does no one see about this layer of the value segment that you provide that everyone should see?
zh: 关于你们所提供的价值链的这一层,有什么是没人看到但每个人都应该看到的?

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we not know?
zh: 我们不知道什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think the big aspect is that not all inference providers are created equal.
zh: 我认为最主要的一点是,并非所有推理提供商都是生而平等的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you have like, you know, great open source projects like, you know, SGLang and VLLM.
zh: 我的意思是,你知道的,有像 SGLang 和 VLLM 这样很棒的开源项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, there are ways to, you know, those are very generalized or generalizable.
zh: 但是,你知道的,这些项目是非常通用化的或者说可泛化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you look at like an inference provider like Fireworks.
zh: 当你看到像 Fireworks 这样的推理提供商时。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fireworks is great.
zh: Fireworks 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've done an incredibly great job.
zh: 他们做得非常出色。

en: Look, I think there are multiple layers across the stack that Crusoe competes with.

speaker: Unknown
en: What do they have that you don't by being specialized?

en: I think there are certain workloads that, you know, Fireworks, you know, does an incredibly great job serving.
zh: 我认为有某些工作负载,你知道的,Fireworks,你知道的,在服务上做得非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, you know, the user experience, I think is something that is unique across all of these different inference platforms that, you know, people may like more on one than the other.
zh: 我认为,你知道的,用户体验,我认为是所有这些不同推理平台上独特的东西,你知道的,人们可能更喜欢其中一个胜过另一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a suite of different tools that, you know, people are, you know, there's a whole bunch of different features that people basically provide across, you know.
zh: 有一整套不同的工具,你知道的,人们,你知道的,基本上提供了大量不同的功能,你知道的,遍布各处。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's nothing like you're, ah, I wish I was them because then we could do this.

speaker: Unknown
en: I sort of come back to this notion of, you know, the oil and gas analogy where the, if you look at the value chain, there are different places where you can compete and there are different places where you can collaborate.
zh: 我某种程度上又回到这个概念,你知道的,石油和天然气的类比,如果你看价值链,有不同的地方可以竞争,也有不同的地方可以协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: When Exxon is pumping wells at the wellhead, they may compete with another upstream oil and gas company to most efficiently drill and operate wells.

speaker: Unknown
en: But they may sell to those same customers if they're building a midstream pipeline to transport oil from the wellhead to the refinery.

speaker: Unknown
en: They may provide capacity in that pipeline to other folks that they're competing with.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, again, I think it comes down to this perspective that I just view there are so many more ways for us to work with folks across the AI infrastructure stack than compete with them.
zh: 所以,再强调一次,我认为归结为这样一个观点:我仅仅认为,与在 AI 基础设施技术栈上与人们竞争相比,我们与他们合作的方式要多得多。

zh: 我能问你一下吗,当你看开源与闭源时,鉴于你从托管推理的角度所拥有的视野,关于资金、token 在开源与闭源之间的分布,你看到了什么,鉴于你拥有的这个独特视角?

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that people are spending more money on closed source frontier models than they are on open source, but they are generating more tokens on open source than closed source.

speaker: Unknown
en: We think open source is actually going to be very important, very valuable.

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's far more private data that's untapped that can actually lead to massive performance gains.
